title: AI agents blowing up IT budgets
full_text:
A new wave of artificial intelligence sticker shock is about to hit businesses, with costs set to soar in the so-called agentic era, risking blowing up productivity savings the much-hyped technology promises to deliver.
That’s according to consulting titan Accenture, which has issued the warning as the Albanese government expects AI to inject up to $600bn a year into the national economy by 2030.
Companies have been burning their AI budgets within months, fuelling what is known as tokenomics. Even big tech has struggled, with Uber spending its entire allocation with Claude maker Anthropic within four months, while Microsoft cancelled most of its internal Claude licences and directed staff to use GitHub Copilot instead.
The runaway costs stem from token-based pricing – or paying for every chunk of text an AI model handles. And it’s been costing some companies thousands of dollars per employee a month, with many failing to see the return on investment.
Accenture AI and data lead Stacy Pence said it was set to get worse as businesses moved from using chatbots to semi or full autonomous agents. Driven by multi-step chained calls, expanding context loops, and repeated retrieval operations, agents consume computational capacity at a rate that threatens to eclipse previous IT overruns.
Compounding the problem, Ms Pence said most companies had little oversight on whether their staff were using expensive AI models for certain tasks when a cheaper one could do the job.
“People don’t even understand what the definition of a token is,” she said. “A token is three quarters of a word and then what you’ve got to understand is that agents use six times the amount of words a human uses. So when you’re using those tools within agents … there is a lack of understanding of how you actually measure that token usage, which is why you see these blowouts.” According to Accenture’s Tokenomics report, agentic workflows currently account for 11 per cent of enterprise token spend. But they represent the fastest-growing category due to their iterative operational nature.
As these workflows grow in complexity, cost curves outpace user growth, rendering static annual IT budgets obsolete.
Ms Pence said without proactive governance, autonomous execution loops could exhaust annual token budgets in mere months – as happened to Uber.
“The way in which the pricing was laid out, in a way the CFO would have understood, they didn’t have the guardrails and such in place,” she said.
“There’s enough of those horror stories out there now that every organisation I’m working with is slowing down and making sure they’ve got the right governance and the right understanding of when they can turn those things off, so they’re not blowing through those budgets.” Accenture research reveals that over half of enterprise AI requests are routed to expensive frontier models, even though 90 per cent of typical workplace tasks do not require frontier-class reasoning. When multi-step agentic workflows default to these top-tier models, cumulative costs rapidly spiral out of control.
